newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA DECLARES TB NATIONAL HEALTH PRIORITY.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA DECLARES TB NATIONAL HEALTH PRIORITY.

text.p: Health Minister Nkosazana Zuma on Thursday declared the fight against tuberculosis (TB) a national priority, saying South Africa had more sufferers than any other country.
"South Africa is facing the worst TB epidemic in the world...more people die of TB in this country than from all other infectious diseases," she told a news briefing.
"If current trends continue 3.5 million people will become sick with TB in the next 10 years," she added.
Zuma said the government was redoubling its efforts to combat the disease.
Health department statistics show that 20,000 people are infected with the disease each year in the Western Cape -- the worst-hit province in the country.
Nobel peace laureate Desmond Tutu, who suffered from the disease when he was younger, said he was proof it could be cured.
"When I was sick nobody would have needed a skeleton to study anatomy. I was living proof," he said.
"I was in hospital for almost two years, but the fact that I am here is proof that the disease is curable," Tutu told the news briefing.
